policy: Six genuine cohort agents; eight distinct bounded missions each. Agent count is not evidence independence.

missions.question: Source-indexed categories and Grothendieck fibrations
missions.assignment: Study source/basis-indexed proof categories, pullback and pushforward, and the conditions allowing proofs to transport across genuine changes in the carrier. Begin with `covariant_proof_descent.py`, `field_context_descent.py`, and the causal Lean modules. Find a Beck–Chevalley-style exact law or a minimal counterexample.
missions.proof_state: LEAN-KERNEL PROVED (repair/base change); PROVED LOCAL (belief transport)

missions.question: Restricted Yoneda and observer adequacy
missions.assignment: Determine when an available probe family separates source objects, morphisms, histories, or proof-support classes. Analyze `yoneda.py` and `operational_yoneda_descent.py`. Distinguish a faithful restricted Yoneda embedding from a merely suggestive collection of observations.

missions.question: Sheafification and observational gluing
missions.assignment: Investigate whether local observational histories admit descent and gluing into a coherent global model. Use `constructive_gluing_tower.py`, `local_global_descent.py`, and source-aware model fusion. Construct a genuine failed-gluing Čech-style obstruction.

missions.question: Nonabelian holonomy and obstruction classes
missions.assignment: Extend graph voltage and permutation holonomy toward groupoid-valued cocycles, nonabelian cohomology, gauge equivalence, and source-sensitive proof transport. Formalize one real obstruction theorem; preserve the distinction between a section existing upstairs and descending downstairs.

missions.question: Kan extensions and representation migration
missions.assignment: Explore whether changing the available observation language admits a universal extension or restriction of models. Test left/right Kan extension candidates against existing source-typed categorical capsules and build explicit failure cases.

missions.question: Universal minimal repair
missions.assignment: Investigate whether observational repair is a reflector, coreflector, closure operator, or only a source-dependent partial construction. Characterize exact existence and idempotence hypotheses; actively seek counterexamples to overly general adjoint claims.

missions.question: Bicategories of instrument histories
missions.assignment: Construct source-changing instruments as 1-morphisms and law-preserving comparisons as 2-morphisms. Determine where noncommuting causal paths, provenance, and report equivalence enter coherence laws. Verify actual horizontal/vertical composition rather than drawing suggestive squares.

missions.question: Lawvere-enriched observation geometry
missions.assignment: Treat distinguishability cost, temporal debt, resource barriers, and resolution as possible enriched-category hom-values. Determine precisely which triangle inequalities and functorial contraction statements survive, and which resource models violate them.

missions.question: Fully formalize VOYAGER's profinite theorem
missions.assignment: Extend `formal/EODCS_Voyager*.lean` to the actual inverse-limit/closure statement with an appropriate pinned topology library. Distinguish formal kernel verification from the existing pen-and-paper topological proof. Demonstrate a compact positive control.

missions.question: Source actualization versus mathematical completion
missions.assignment: Seek necessary and sufficient source-image closedness conditions beyond finite and compact cases. Investigate Polish, locally compact, Baire, and effective source spaces, and test nonclosed countermodels.

missions.question: Effective versus classical finite refutation
missions.assignment: The current finite-source theorem uses classical choice to select witnesses. Investigate computable probe enumeration, decidability, recursively enumerable evidence, resource bounds, and explicit examples where a finite witness exists but cannot be extracted uniformly by the available procedure.

missions.question: Domain theory and partial observation
missions.assignment: Model partial evidence using information orders, Scott topology, directed joins, and continuous update maps. Characterize when an ideal limit contains legitimate partial information without manufacturing a completed source.

missions.question: Gödel, reflection, and \(\omega+1\)
missions.assignment: Analyze `godel_succ.py`, `ordinal_succ_report.py`, and `checkpoint_meta_tower.py`. Separate finite proof transport, reflection, consistency statements, limit-stage models, and physically performed computations. Target a new precise bridge theorem with strict Gödel/Turing guardrails.
missions.proof_state: CLASSICAL / PROVED LOCAL; support lemma LEAN-KERNEL PROVED

missions.question: Descriptive-set complexity of observer properties
missions.assignment: Classify eventual-zero, infinitely-many-ones, eventual-periodicity, and related source properties by their finite-cylinder or Borel structure. Derive exact finite-observation decidability criteria; retain the distinction between topological nondecidability and logical independence.

missions.question: Final coalgebras and behavioral equivalence
missions.assignment: Connect deterministic, relational, stochastic, and history-dependent observers using coalgebraic semantics. Identify which existing SUCC quotients really arise from final semantics and which require additional structure.

missions.question: Generalized memory debt
missions.assignment: Extend VOYAGER's \(2^k\) pulse-gap source-state lower bound to periodic markers, nested sparse sequences, arbitrary finite alphabets, and multi-action distinguishability. Seek sharp minimal-automaton state counts, not only lower bounds.
missions.proof_state: PROVED LOCAL; marker lemma LEAN-KERNEL PROVED

missions.question: Stochastic source-changing fibrations
missions.assignment: Build an indexed theory of original state, current carrier, intervention, observation history, and conditional law. Derive genuine composition and source-provenance laws. Do not infer probabilities from support alone.

missions.question: Bayesian gluing and commuting updates
missions.assignment: Compare the conditional-product results in sibling PR #45 with EODCS's Fréchet intervals. Identify exact assumptions under which Bayes updates commute with shared-source gluing; independently reproduce the duplicated-evidence counterexample.

missions.question: Quantum instrument histories
missions.assignment: Extend `quantum_records.py` toward finite completely positive instrument composition, state disturbance, source-history retention, and distinguishability after readout. Separate quantum states, recorded outcomes, and semantic claims.

missions.question: Blackwell sufficiency and experimental informativeness
missions.assignment: Connect observer refinements to statistical experiments and stochastic garbling orders. Find necessary/sufficient conditions for one observer to simulate another under a common source, and provide noncomparable experiment examples.

missions.question: Adaptive observation-policy mathematics
missions.assignment: Generalize AND/OR proof-policy fixed points to uncertain original sources, destructive instruments, finite costs, and adversarial hidden states. Seek optimal-policy existence and impossibility certificates that do not silently assume resets.

missions.question: Distributed and concurrent causal receipts
missions.assignment: Replace totally ordered reports with causally partially ordered events. Explore concurrency, trace monoids, dependency graphs, and source-preserving reorderability. Characterize which independent events may commute without losing proof meaning.

missions.question: Martingales and evidence wealth
missions.assignment: Investigate likelihood-ratio martingales, Ville bounds, optional stopping, data-processing inequalities, and dependent evidence. Determine exactly what source-calibrated sequential confidence can establish—and why it cannot replace a mathematical proof.

missions.question: Information erasure versus physical cost
missions.assignment: Relate entropy loss, measurement backaction, memory requirements, and Landauer-type limits. Distinguish exact information-theoretic inequalities from claims requiring a thermodynamic physical model and temperature/energy assumptions.

missions.question: Logistic-map observational chaos
missions.assignment: Revisit `logistic_observer_tree.py` and `chaos_source_quotient.py`. Under what exact probe language can chaotic source dynamics admit simple observer dynamics? Prove a quotient theorem, then seek a mutation that destroys it.

missions.question: Renormalization and symbolic dynamics
missions.assignment: Connect bifurcation, kneading sequences, shift spaces, and renormalization to hierarchical observer frontiers. Determine whether source-depth and observation-depth transformations commute.
missions.proof_state: BLOCKED (broad renormalization); PROVED LOCAL (typed shift square)

missions.question: Koopman and Perron–Frobenius operators
missions.assignment: Explore the linear representation of nonlinear dynamics and the conditions under which an observational quotient is a closed invariant subspace or factor. Provide an explicit lossy-observation countermodel.

missions.question: Lyapunov exponents and epistemic resolution debt
missions.assignment: Study finite-time growth of distinguishability, error amplification, metric entropy, and observer precision. Derive a resource/observation horizon bound with real hypotheses, not a universal slogan that “chaos creates information.”

missions.question: Attractors, Conley-type invariants, and self-update events
missions.assignment: Investigate local deflection versus structural reconstruction as mathematically distinct dynamical events. Search for invariant sets or connection matrices preserved under lawful observer maps.

missions.question: PDE filtering and closure
missions.assignment: Use the existing Maxwell/Lorentz work and relevant Navier–Stokes/LES mathematics to study projection-induced closure terms. Preserve the exact negative control \(P(w\otimes w)\ne0\) even when \(Pw=0\). Do not claim global NS regularity.

missions.question: Covariant observers and causal cones
missions.assignment: Study `relativistic_shadow_tower.py`, `galilean_lorentz_succ.py`, and observer-frame transport. Distinguish covariance of mathematical reports, finite causal accessibility, and actual spacetime physics.

missions.question: Delay-coordinate embeddings
missions.assignment: Compare Takens-style state reconstruction with SUCC's generated future probes. Find hypotheses under which time-delayed observations genuinely recover the source, and adversarial cases where they fundamentally fail.

missions.question: The affine SUCC/FUCC algebra
missions.assignment: Study the exact relation \(V_pS=S^pV_p\), ax+b semigroups, crossed products, groupoid constructions, and faithful representations. Preserve noncommuting cross-terms before quotienting.
missions.proof_state: PROVED LOCAL; affine lemmas LEAN-KERNEL PROVED

missions.question: Prime jets, valuation geometry, and factor-square dynamics
missions.assignment: Revisit prime-power rays, valuation coordinates, the diagonal carrier, square-root cones, and moving factor windows. Search for source-faithful invariants coupling additive and multiplicative motion.

missions.question: Prime clocks, Mahler expansions, and \(p\)-adic interpolation
missions.assignment: Investigate valuation clocks, Kummer congruences, finite differences, CRT synchronization, and extension from finite clocks to \(p\)-adic analytic objects. Identify the actual regularity needed for interpolation.

missions.question: Dirichlet logarithms and multiplicativity
missions.assignment: Characterize which source interactions disappear or survive under arithmetic convolution logarithms. Always test fake composite impulses, non-Euler coefficient models, and altered prime phases.

missions.question: The Archimedean Gamma boundary
missions.assignment: Analyze the relation among the SUCC ladder, Mellin transforms, Gamma factors, trivial-zero cancellation, and local finite approximations. Prove legitimate identities and explicitly expose unsupported analytic-continuation jumps.

missions.question: Arithmetic polarization and Weil/Suzuki
missions.assignment: Attack the distinction between cheap positive covariance and the actual completed source-derived Weil pairing. Try to construct a legitimate operator/polarization bridge—or rigorously kill candidate bridges with completed Gamma, half-density, phase, and topology controls.

missions.question: Gaussian primes and arithmetic holonomy
missions.assignment: Revisit Gaussian-prime graph walks, finite moat certificates, voltage transport, path-groupoid obstructions, and source completeness. Find a theorem connecting transport certificates to the actual arithmetic graph, with negative mutation controls.

missions.question: Spectral dynamics and virtual zeros
missions.assignment: Explore dynamic Fourier, transfer operators, Hankel kernels, Mellin/Fourier duality, and observer-dependent spectral artifacts. Determine which apparent zero motions are basis/projection artifacts and which are genuine source-invariant information.

missions.question: Parallel-branch mathematical triangulation
missions.assignment: Independently audit PR #45 versus PRs #44–#48. Compare proofs, CEGIS mechanisms, source contracts, discoveries, and failed paths. Investigate the learned order-\(p^3\) Heisenberg-type action invariant as a bridge to holonomy and noncommuting observation.

missions.question: Grammar-expanding genetic mathematics
missions.assignment: Evolve not merely candidate constants or bijections, but typed mathematical constructors: quotients, group actions, natural transformations, adjunctions, completions, connections, and proof languages. Require semantic verification at every mutation boundary.

missions.question: Unknown-target invariant discovery
missions.assignment: Train on independent source tables with opaque labels, then seal genuinely independent mathematical holdouts. See whether the learner can infer invariant structure rather than memorize a presentation. Track exactly what the programmer supplied.

missions.question: No-free-lunch and identifiability frontiers
missions.assignment: Investigate when any amount of model proliferation or computation is impotent because the permitted source experiments identify the same observational equivalence class. Seek minimal certificates for genuinely novel instrument requirements.

missions.question: Proof debt, Zeno effects, and scheduler theory
missions.assignment: Study source-changing proof cost, expanding observation horizons, and knowledge/debt growth. Distinguish an intrinsically divergent cost law from a poorly scheduled but finite proof search. Build sharp positive and negative resource bounds.

missions.question: Mathematical phenomenology and TLICA
missions.assignment: Explore self-boundaries, deeply load-bearing model features, prediction errors, semantic coupling, and field reconstruction as abstract dynamical/information structures. Extract defensible mathematics; do not claim this validates human psychology or neuroscience.

missions.question: Collective phase, rhythm, and coordinated observers
missions.assignment: Investigate phase locking, coupled oscillators, shared timing, synchronization, groove/pocket, and collective semantic coherence as mathematical phenomena. Look for structures transferable to multiple SUCC observers without confusing musical metaphors with physical proofs.

missions.question: The flagship moonshot: a sheaf or fibration of lawful causal histories
missions.assignment: Attempt a single theory in which source-changing probes, preparation history, observer states, feasible policies, proof-support transport, and ideal observational limits coexist. Determine its actual objects, morphisms, gluing rules, obstruction classes, and universal properties. Test against all successful results and every major no-go in SUCC.

mission_execution_summary.note: Completed investigation does not mean original conjecture proved. Each proof_state records the earned result; broad D26, E38 and F48 targets remain blocked/open.
